subject: On-prem data handshake: tenant retention, customer keys, and access scopes
messages:
From: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@aurorahealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@aurorahealth.com>, legal@aurorahealth.com
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Initial questions — private deployment, keys, and retention

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking a look at Aurora's private deployment option. Before we advance procurement, the legal and security teams asked me to confirm a few specific items so we can sign the DPA and move to SOW:  

1) Customer-managed keys (CMK): We need confirmation you support HSM-backed KEKs where Aurora holds the root key in our KMS and Redwood only receives wrapped keys for runtime. Can you describe the handshake, rotation, and redelivery process?  

2) Operator access and breakglass: What operational access, if any, do Redwood engineers retain for on-prem/VPC deploys? Please include conditions (legal process, incident response), how access is logged, and the party that holds the revocation controls.  

3) Data retention and e-discovery: Our retention policy requires the ability to place legal holds and export a tenant’s data within 72 hours. Is there a supported process (technical + contractual) for data exports from a private deployment?  

4) Cross-border transfers & subprocessors: Confirm whether any telemetry, observability, or support tooling sends metadata outside the EU/US for our configured region. Please attach a current subprocessors list and proposed DPA annex language.

I attached a short checklist Aurora uses for vendor on-prem deployments (aurora-request-checklist.xlsx). If it helps, we can schedule a short 30-minute call this week to walk through.

Regards,
Sarah Mills
Senior Counsel — Aurora Health
attachments: aurora-request-checklist.xlsx
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial questions — private deployment, keys, and retention

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. I copied Priyom (security/infrastructure) and Lauren (legal) and summarized our posture below. I've attached a draft DPA tailored for private deployments and a KEK handshake diagram.

Short answers up front:  
- CMK: Yes — we support customer-controlled KEKs. KEKs are HSM-wrapped; Redwood receives only wrapped keys. We support automated rotation where Aurora triggers rewrap via KMS API and Redwood relies on rewrapped keys. We can include an experimental KEK redelivery procedure for emergency recovery (detailed in the attached draft).
- Operator access: By default, Redwood engineers have zero direct key access for private VPC/on-prem installs. Operator activities (support bundles, traces) are gated by breakglass that requires written authorization plus a signed court/order or escalation to Aurora security ops. All operator actions are logged to customer-controlled logging endpoints.
- Retention & e-discovery: We support tenant-level exports via an API that can be executed by Aurora's administrators; for private deployments we can commit contractually to a 72-hour export SLA. We'll include the export API and legal-hold flow in the DPA annex.
- Subprocessors & telemetry: For the US region we do not route tenant data outside the configured VPC. Minimal telemetry (service health pings and anonymized metrics) can be disabled; we will provide the subprocessors list and an annex restricting telemetry endpoints.

Proposed next steps:  
1) We redline the attached DPA with the explicit KEK and breakglass language.
2) Schedule a technical call (Priyom + your infra lead) to review the KEK handshake and export API.
3) Finalize Annex B (subprocessors) and confirm DocuSign path.

Attachments: redwood-dpa-privdep-proposal-2028-08-28.pdf; kek-handshake-diagram-aurora.png

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Privacy & Governance — Redwood Inference
From: Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@aurorahealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: legal@aurorahealth.com
Date: Thu, 23 Aug 2028 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial questions — private deployment, keys, and retention

Priya — thanks for the quick response. Couple of follow-ups from procurement/legal:  

> On Wed, Aug 22, 2028 at 12:40 PM Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
> > We can include an experimental KEK redelivery procedure for emergency recovery (detailed in the attached draft).

1) Escrow / redelivery: Procurement wants clearer SLAs for key redelivery and escrow triggers. If Aurora has to exercise escrow (e.g., provider insolvency, court order), what is the precisely defined timeline and method? We prefer a written escrow with a third-party custodian.
2) Breakglass audit: We need detailed audit log retention (minimum 7 years) and a process for redacted copies for regulators.
3) E-discovery chain-of-custody: The 72-hour export SLA is good; we also require a declaration of exported file formats and a checksum-based integrity statement.

Can you add these as redline items? If possible, include a separate escrow addendum we can circulate internally.

—Aaron
Aaron Cole
Counsel, Procurement — Aurora Health
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@aurorahealth.com>, Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial questions — private deployment, keys, and retention

All — putting in draft redlines and a short technical summary so Aurora can see exactly how the handshake works and the operator constraints. See the attached technical appendix in the DPA draft. Key points we implemented in the draft:  

- Customer KEK model: KEK remains under Aurora's KMS; Redwood only receives wrapped session keys. KEK rotation is API-driven; rotation events are signed by Aurora and logged.
- Escrow: We can agree to a third-party escrow custodian for a sealed KEK-release process. Suggested SLA for KEK release: 5 business days after receipt of jointly-agreed legal trigger and custodian verification. We explicitly call out custodial responsibilities in the annex.
- Breakglass: Operator access is implemented as a privileged workflow requiring (1) authenticated Aurora incident ticket, (2) Aurora-signed authorization token, and (3) court order OR Aurora security ops approval. All actions generate tamper-evident logs shipped to Aurora's logging endpoint.
- Export/E-discovery: Export API produces a zipped export (JSONL for records, AES-256 encrypted) with a SHA256 checksum. We commit to 72-hour window for successful export initiation; completion depends on dataset size but we commit to staged transfer guarantees and integrity proofs.

I'm attaching: redwood-dpa-privdep-proposal-2028-08-28.pdf (draft with technical annex) and kek-handshake-diagram-aurora.png. Lauren — I left comments where legal should add specific escrow and audit language per Aaron's ask.

—Priyom
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

Sarah / Aaron —

Thanks again for the detailed asks. We've updated the DPA draft and annexes per the thread and added an escrow addendum with a suggested third-party custodian (details in Annex C). Highlights in the revised package (attached):  

• KEK escrow: proposed custodian + KEK-release flow + 5-business-day SLA after verified trigger.
• Breakglass: operator workflow and mandatory Aurora-signed authorization token; immutable audit log retention defined (7 years, with redaction process for regulator requests).
• Export: API export format (JSONL), AES-256 envelope encryption, SHA256 checksums, 72-hour initiation SLA.
• Subprocessors: explicit denylist for telemetry endpoints; full subprocessors roster included.

Next steps we propose:  
1) Technical call — Priyom and Aurora infra lead (30 minutes). Suggested window: Thu 08/31 or Mon 09/04.
2) Once tech call confirms the handshake, we circulate the final DPA + Annex C for signature (DocuSign link included).

Links & attachments: redwood-dpa-privdep-proposal-2028-08-28.pdf; kek-handshake-diagram-aurora.png; https://hubspot.com/deals/AUR-2028-004; https://app.docusign.com/recipient/XYZ

Best regards,
Priya Natarajan
